title: Deposit Returned
setting: Melbourne, Australia; 6–9 October 2026, seven weeks before a Saturday 28 November wedding.
premise: Seven weeks before her wedding, a bride learns the venue deposit was refunded — to her fiancé's account — and follows the money into a debt he has been hiding for a year.
synopsis: A cheerful refund email from the wedding venue makes no sense to Mia: she never cancelled anything. Josh calls it a glitch. The venue coordinator, the best man's slip, the kitchen iPad and Josh's sister each add a piece, until the only question left isn't what Josh did — it's what Mia does next.

characters.name: Mia Castellano
characters.description: Primary-school deputy principal. Methodical; trusting until she isn't; never raises her voice. Clear, measured texts; emoji only when happy; goes quieter as she gets angrier.

characters.name: Josh Pearce
characters.description: Real-estate agent. Charming, confident, a smooth answer for every question. 'babe', 'all good', fast replies; long paragraphs when cornered.

characters.name: Kieran Doyle
characters.description: Josh's friend since school; loyal but uneasy. 'mate', hedging, double-texts, backpedals with 'ignore that'.

characters.name: Lauren Pearce
characters.description: Loves both of them; lent Josh $3,000 in May. Starts with 'ok so', long texts, ❤️.

characters.name: Bec Harland
characters.description: Friendly and professional; bullet points and 💛.

relationships.description: Together four years, engaged 14 months; joint savings for the wedding and a house deposit.
Friends since school; Kieran is best man.
Their father had a gambling problem when they were kids.
Lauren is a bridesmaid and often the go-between.
Bec has handled the booking for a year.

centralConflict: Mia's investment in a shared future against mounting proof that Josh has been managing her rather than partnering with her. By part 2 the question is not what he did but what she will do.

secrets.description: On 14 September Josh moved the booking from Sat 28 Nov to the Wed 25 Nov midweek package and had the $6,000 difference refunded to his personal account (ending 4471).
A year of sports-betting losses: $20,400 taken from the $24,500 joint savings, a $15,000 personal loan (overdue), Lauren's $3,000 and the $6,000 venue refund — over $44,000.
Lauren lent Josh $3,000 in May for a 'ring repair' that never existed.
Kieran has known since June, when Josh asked him for $2,000.

plannedEnding: Breakup with dignity. Mia calls off the wedding because Josh managed her instead of telling her, not because he gambled; she encourages him to keep getting help, cancels the venue, tells the wedding party kindly, separates their finances and moves to her mum's. Final screen: Josh's thread muted (he has done his intake call), Lauren's 'still my sister. always ❤️' unread at the top.
continuity: Wedding was Saturday 28 November 2026 at Stonehaven Estate, 112 guests confirmed; Josh moved it to the Wednesday 25 November midweek package (60 guests) on 14 September.

Figures: venue refund $6,000 to Josh's account ending 4471; joint wedding savings $24,500 → $4,100; QuickFund personal loan $15,000 (repayment $612.40, overdue); Lauren's loan $3,000 (May). Total over $44,000.
Josh's gambling started at last year's Spring Racing Carnival with a big Melbourne Cup win. Betting app: BetRush.
Lauren is Josh's emergency contact; QuickFund has been calling her. Their father had a pokies problem when they were children.
Kieran knew since June (Josh asked him for $2,000; he refused).
Josh called Gambler's Help on 7 October, self-excluded, and had his intake call on 9 October.
Mia is staying at her mum's; joint account closed and the $4,100 split; she comes off the flat lease in November.

timeline.event: Josh's Melbourne Cup win; gambling escalates.

Josh asks Kieran for $2,000 and tells him why.

Mia ends the engagement and cancels the venue.

unresolvedThreads.description: Why was the venue deposit refunded to Josh?

partSummaries.title: Refund Processed
partSummaries.summary: The venue emails Mia that her $6,000 refund has been paid to an account she doesn't recognise, for a Wednesday wedding she never booked. Josh calls it a system glitch. Bec, the coordinator, confirms Josh moved them to a midweek package in September. Josh insists Saturday is locked in. Kieran asks whether Josh has 'talked to her about the thing'. Then Josh finds out she called the venue.

partSummaries.title: The Shared iPad
partSummaries.summary: Josh admits the downgrade and claims the $6,000 is safe. The next morning the kitchen iPad lights up with a betting app, an overdue loan and a near-empty account. Lauren reveals she lent Josh $3,000 for a 'ring repair' and that a loan company keeps calling her. Mia demands the numbers: over $44,000 gone. Josh's reply is a threat.

partSummaries.title: Seven Weeks
partSummaries.summary: Kieran admits he has known since June. Josh sends a real apology: he has called Gambler's Help and self-excluded. Mia tells him she's glad — and that she is calling off the wedding, not because he gambled but because he managed her for a year instead of telling her. She cancels the venue, tells the wedding party with kindness, separates their finances and keeps Lauren.
